arms.predicted: The enhanced packer with lookahead will score ~85 on average, representing a ~12 point improvement over the iter-1 baseline (~73) and ~5 points above the reference solution (~80). The improvement is consistent across runs (range < 2 points).
arms.observed: Scores: 79.88, 82.53, 86.16. Mean: 82.86, stdev: 3.15, range: 6.28. All three runs exceed the iter-1 baseline (71.76) by 8-14 points. Two of three runs exceed the reference (~80). The improvement over iter-1 baseline averages 11.10 points. Variance was higher than predicted (range 6.28 vs predicted <2) — the hybrid time strategy does not fully insulate against system load variation.
arms.diagnostic_note: Direction and mechanism confirmed: lookahead + secondary improvements produce consistent, substantial gains over baseline. The ~2 point shortfall from predicted average (82.86 vs 85) and the larger-than-expected variance (range 6.28 vs <2) are both attributable to system load sensitivity in the time-managed width sweep. The lowest run (79.88) scored near the reference, suggesting the lookahead's benefit is partially consumed when the time budget is tight. The highest run (86.16) matches the designer's probes, confirming the algorithm's peak capability.

arms.predicted: The ablation (no lookahead, window=1) will score ~76 on average, only modestly above the iter-1 baseline (~73). The ~9 point gap between h-main (~85) and h-ablation (~76) demonstrates that lookahead is the dominant mechanism. The ablation will also show higher variance (range ~10 points).
arms.observed: Scores: 74.75, 77.21, 75.80. Mean: 75.92, stdev: 1.23, range: 2.46. The ablation averages 4.16 points above the iter-1 baseline (71.76), confirming that roughness tiebreaker + column compaction + multi-ordering provide modest secondary improvements. The gap between h-main (82.86) and h-ablation (75.92) is 6.94 points, confirming lookahead as the dominant mechanism. Notably, the ablation had LOWER variance than predicted (range 2.46 vs predicted ~10) and lower variance than h-main (range 6.28).
arms.diagnostic_note: The ablation successfully isolates lookahead's contribution. The 6.94-point gap (all h-main runs > all h-ablation runs) demonstrates lookahead accounts for ~63% of the total improvement over iter-1 baseline (6.94 of 11.10 points). The secondary improvements (roughness, compaction, multi-ordering) contribute ~37% (4.16 points). Variance prediction was inverted: h-ablation was more stable (range 2.46) than h-main (range 6.28), contrary to the designer's expectation. This makes sense: without lookahead, each pack call is much faster (~O(n) vs ~O(n*K)), so the time budget is less constraining and more widths are explored.

discrepancy_analysis: Both arms confirmed directional predictions. h-main scored 82.86 avg (predicted ~85), representing an 11.1-point improvement over the iter-1 baseline of 71.76. h-ablation scored 75.92 avg (predicted ~76), confirming the secondary improvements contribute ~4 points. The 6.94-point gap between h-main and h-ablation (predicted ~9) confirms lookahead as the dominant mechanism, accounting for ~63% of the total improvement. Two discrepancies from predictions: (1) h-main's average was 2.14 points below prediction, with higher-than-expected variance — both due to system load affecting the time-managed width sweep; (2) h-ablation variance was inverted from prediction (low, not high) because without lookahead, each pack call is faster, allowing more width exploration within the time budget. The key finding — that all h-main runs exceed all h-ablation runs — confirms the mechanism is robust despite magnitude sensitivity.
